text:
jordan: rolling out the kernel-selector tweak from yesterday and we see a 12-18% p95 tail regression on TRT-vLLM runs. attaching nsys and perfetto slices.

mei: ugh okay. is this across all sequence lengths or just long tails? do you have a quick nvprof/nsys flame snapshot?

jordan: short/long both, but tails worse for concat-heavy prompts. here's the nsys link: https://internal.artifacts/nsys/2083456789/trace.qdrep and a tiny extracted timeline: 
```
CPU: wrapper thread blocked 84ms waiting on GPU stream (many small gaps)
GPU: dozens of tiny kernel launches (0.2-1.5ms) with 10-25us host-side enqueue latency
Scheduler: batching decision serializes on a single mutex at ~500Hz
```

sam: that host enqueue latency + serial mutex smells like the wrapper is doing per-request kernel selection on the hot path instead of caching the choice. did the selector change invalidate the kernel-lookups?

jordan: exactly. we moved kernel selection into the wrapper init for each inference instead of reusing per-engine selection. commit ref: a1b2c3d. i can repro locally with a small harness.

ana: can we get a KV cache heatmap? if wrapper stalls while prefetching KV pages you'll amplify enqueue spikes.

jordan: pasted a perfetto flame cropped to the invoke window: 
```
00:00:00.000 wrapper: acquire mutex (0.35ms)
00:00:00.350 selector: warmup kernel pick (0.70ms)
00:00:01.020 prefetch: KV miss fetch (1.4ms) -> memcpy
00:00:02.420 launch: tensorrt::enqueue (0.4-0.8ms) repeated 40x
```

mei: so two problems: selector on-hot-path + KV prefetch blocking the CPU that enqueues kernels. both multiply the enqueue jitter. can you try: 1) move selector to engine-attach time, 2) make KV prefetch async (background worker), and 3) add a lightweight spinless token for batching decisions?

jordan: testing those now. initial patch (selector cached) drops host-side enqueue latency from median 180us -> 35us on my rig. p95 on end-to-end drops ~10%. will run nsys full sweep.

perf-bot: automated-profile summary for 2083456789: 
- total host enqueue overhead: 14.2% of request CPU time
- blocking waits in wrapper thread: 92ms per 1000 requests
- kernel_launch_count increased by 28% for short prompts after selector change
(see https://ci.profiles/2083456789/summary) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: nice. once we land the selector cache + async prefetch we should add a microtest that verifies enqueue latency < 100us for 95th percentile and kernel selection not on critical path.

ana: also add a perf regression alert to the pipeline so any future change that increases kernel_launch_count by >15% fails CI.

jordan: agreed. i'll open PR with perf results and the microtest. linking draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4247 :eyes: 

mei: thanks. if the nsys full-sweep confirms, we can cut a quick patch release to Dedicated pools to stop the regression. :thumbsup:

sam: quick note — when you run the wide nsys sweep, include a trace with NVTX annotations around batching decisions and engine.enqueue to make the host/GPU boundary obvious in perfetto. saved us last time.

jordan: will do. thanks all.
